analysis_validation.method: local equation-equivalent reproduction of milgrau.level2.kfs productive Monte Carlo using product-resolved parameters
analysis_validation.interpretation: The analysis path exactly reproduced persisted productive block backscatter means and standard deviations on supported bins before experimental boundaries were tested.

candidate_design.principle: No composite score and no altitude target is used as a productive gate. Two explicit probes are compared plus one graceful-failure stress diagnostic.

moderate_probe.definition: accepted in all five blocks and nearest 10 km, used only to probe a higher-boundary regime

support_edge_probe.definition: highest candidate accepted in all five blocks whose nominal exact backward path has complete finite positive signal/error/molecular support in all five blocks

extreme_high_graceful_failure_probe.definition: highest candidate accepted in all five blocks regardless of backward path completeness; used to test whether candidate acceptance alone is a usable KFS boundary

355.finding: Local candidate QA/persistence does not imply a usable exact KFS boundary; non-positive center/path bins terminate backward support.

532.finding: Even with positive center bins, internal non-positive path bins prevent a contiguous backward inversion to the lower column.

interpretation: The experiment reproduces productive method-v4 numerical outputs before changing the boundary, so observed differences are attributable to the experimental boundary choice/estimator under the stated model.
A higher locally accepted and temporally persistent Rayleigh candidate is not sufficient for a backward KFS boundary because full contiguous inversion support is a separate requirement.

The support-edge probes are nominally path-complete but become highly fragile under the existing 300-member uncertainty perturbations: only a minority of exact-boundary simulations and approximately 0.3% of fitted-boundary simulations remain complete in the worst blocks.

The 10-km moderate probe remains substantially more stable, but 355-nm fitted/exact experiments can still lose at least one Monte Carlo realization under current all-simulations-valid productive semantics.
Differences from method v4 are regression/sensitivity differences, not truth errors; a smaller difference from method v4 does not validate an experimental boundary estimator.
No interpolation or gap bridging is introduced. The extreme-high cases are retained as graceful support-failure evidence rather than forced retrievals.
decision: Do not promote a high boundary, fitted boundary, hard SNR threshold or method v5. Current evidence shows that contiguous path support and perturbation robustness become limiting before the highest shape-QA/persistent candidates.
next_gate: characterize why Monte Carlo perturbations break path completeness near 10-12 km and whether this is dominated by single-bin weak-signal tails or dependence assumptions
add correlated-noise/leave-part-out tests and preserve strict no-gap semantics
repeat on a materially different SPU case before deriving any rule
only then decide whether vertical aggregation or another declared-resolution strategy merits a second high-boundary experiment
